[[File:Obama with 2013 MLS Cup winner Sporting Kansas City team October 2014.jpg|thumb|right|[[Sporting Kansas City]], winners of [[MLS Cup 2013]], are hosted by President [[Barack Obama]] at the [[White House]].|alt=A group of soccer players for Sporting Kansas City dressed in suits behind President Barack Obama, who stands at a podium. The MLS Cup trophy stands to the President's left on a table.]]

The [[MLS Cup]] is the annual championship match of [[Major League Soccer]] (MLS), the top-level men's [[association football|soccer]] league for the United States and Canada. The match marks the conclusion of the [[MLS Cup playoffs]], a five-round knockout competition contested by the top nine teams from each of the league's two conferences.<ref>{{cite news |last=Tannenwald |first=Jonathan |date=February 21, 2023 |title=MLS changes its playoff format again, now guaranteeing home games for more teams |url=https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/mls-playoffs-2023-format-schedule-change-20230221.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |accessdate=October 19, 2023 |archive-date=October 16, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016102827/https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/mls-playoffs-2023-format-schedule-change-20230221.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2023 MLS Competition Guidelines |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/about/competition-guidelines |publisher=[[Major League Soccer]] |accessdate=October 19, 2023 |archive-date=May 1, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501233548/https://www.mlssoccer.com/about/competition-guidelines |url-status=live }}</ref> The playoffs tournament is organized by the league at the end of the regular season in a format which is similar to other [[Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada|major professional sports leagues]] in the United States and Canada, but unlike most soccer leagues.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ruthven |first=Graham |date=November 5, 2015 |title=Could MLS-style play-offs work in Europe's top leagues? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/nov/05/mls-playoff-european-football |work=[[The Guardian]] |access-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624204543/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/nov/05/mls-playoff-european-football |archive-date=June 24, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The league also awards the [[Supporters' Shield]] to teams that have the most [[Three points for a win|points]] during the regular season. Both the MLS Cup champion and Supporters' Shield winner qualify for the [[CONCACAF Champions Cup]], contested by the champions of [[CONCACAF]] leagues in North America, Central America, and the Caribbean.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goff |first=Steven |date=December 5, 2015 |title=MLS playoff format is an outlier in world soccer — and that's a good thing |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/soccer-insider/wp/2015/12/05/mls-playoff-format-is-an-outlier-in-world-soccer-and-thats-a-good-thing/?noredirect=on |work=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210111005/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/soccer-insider/wp/2015/12/05/mls-playoff-format-is-an-outlier-in-world-soccer-and-thats-a-good-thing/?noredirect=on |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The MLS Cup champion also qualifies for the [[Campeones Cup]], a friendly held since 2018 against the winners of the Mexican [[Campeón de Campeones]] from [[Liga MX]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Myers |first=Jacob |date=September 27, 2021 |title=A chance for a trophy and a consequential MLS game, Columbus Crew enter biggest week of season |url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/2021/09/27/campeones-cup-and-important-road-game-crew-enter-biggest-week-year/5882383001/ |work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]] |accessdate=January 1, 2023 |archive-date=December 10, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210093454/https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/2021/09/27/campeones-cup-and-important-road-game-crew-enter-biggest-week-year/5882383001/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

First contested in 1996, the MLS Cup was originally hosted by a predetermined [[Neutral venue|neutral site]] selected by the league before the regular season.<ref name="USA-2012">{{cite news |last=Dreier |first=Frederick |date=November 29, 2012 |title=Wild-card L.A. Galaxy favored in home-field MLS Cup |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2012/11/29/galaxy-favored-in-home-field-mls-cup/1735965/ |work=USA Today |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210154624/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2012/11/29/galaxy-favored-in-home-field-mls-cup/1735965/ |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Since the [[MLS Cup 2012|2012 edition]], the match has been hosted by the remaining team with the highest regular season standing.<ref name="USA-2012"/> The final, originally contested in October, was moved to November and later December as the length of the regular season and playoffs were extended by the league.<ref>{{cite news |date=January 5, 2012 |title=MLS reveals 2012 schedule, including MLS Cup in December |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2012/01/05/mls-reveals-2012-schedule-including-mls-cup-december |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=December 12, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215221935/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2012/01/05/mls-reveals-2012-schedule-including-mls-cup-december |archive-date=December 15, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The playoffs originally allowed for lower-ranked seeds, known as [[Wild card (sports)|wild cards]], to be placed into different sides of the bracket regardless of their actual conference. As a result, several MLS Cups have featured two teams from the same conference.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rodriguez |first=Alicia |date=October 21, 2015 |title=Audi MLS Cup Playoffs: Tracing the evolution of the postseason format since 1996 |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2015/10/21/audi-mls-cup-playoffs-tracing-evolution-postseason-format |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181113165913/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2015/10/21/audi-mls-cup-playoffs-tracing-evolution-postseason-format |archive-date=November 13, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Inter Miami CF]] are the reigning cup-holders, having defeated [[Vancouver Whitecaps FC]] in the [[MLS Cup 2025|2025 final]] for their first title. The [[LA Galaxy]] hold the record for most MLS Cup titles, having won six times in ten appearances.<ref name="ESPN-List">{{cite news |last=Jenkins |first=Keith |date=December 6, 2025 |orig-date=originally published December 7, 2024 |title=MLS Cup: All-time winners list, MVP and more stats to know |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/42777641/mls-cup-all-winners-list-mvp-more-stats-know |publisher=ESPN |accessdate=December 7, 2025}}</ref> The championship has been won by the same team in two or more consecutive years on three occasions, and the match has featured consecutive sets of finalists on three occasions.<ref>{{cite news |last=Milles |first=Todd |date=November 30, 2017 |title=Sounders stamp MLS Cup rematch ticket with Toronto |url=https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/soccer/mls/sounders-fc/article187475518.html |work=[[The News Tribune]] |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210154627/https://www.thenewstribune.com/sports/soccer/mls/sounders-fc/article187475518.html |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Five finals have featured two teams participating as finalists for the first time.<ref name="ESPN-List"/><ref>{{cite news |last=Baxter |first=Kevin |date=November 5, 2022 |title=LAFC defeats Philadelphia on penalty kicks to win MLS Cup title in thriller |url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2022-11-05/lafc-defeats-philadelphia-penalty-kicks-mls-title |work=[[Los Angeles Times]] |accessdate=November 5, 2022 |archive-date=February 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230219094040/https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2022-11-05/lafc-defeats-philadelphia-penalty-kicks-mls-title |url-status=live }}</ref> Nine teams have also won "[[Double (association football)|the double]]", claiming the MLS Cup and either the Supporters' Shield, the [[U.S. Open Cup]], or the [[Canadian Championship]] during the same season; only Toronto FC has won a [[Treble (association football)|treble]], having achieved it in 2017.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rodriguez |first=Alicia |date=December 9, 2017 |title=Toronto FC win first domestic treble in MLS history |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2017/12/09/toronto-fc-win-first-domestic-treble-mls-history |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210111230/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2017/12/09/toronto-fc-win-first-domestic-treble-mls-history |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Rodriguez |first=Alicia |date=November 5, 2022 |title=LAFC win MLS Cup, Supporters' Shield double |url=https://www.angelsonparade.com/2022/11/5/23442524/lafc-win-mls-cup-supporters-shield-double |work=Angels on Parade |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=November 5, 2022 |archive-date=November 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221105232619/https://www.angelsonparade.com/2022/11/5/23442524/lafc-win-mls-cup-supporters-shield-double |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Landon Donovan]] has played in seven MLS Cup finals and totaled 726&nbsp;minutes—both competition records.<ref>{{cite news |date=December 7, 2014 |title=LA Galaxy legend Landon Donovan wins MLS record sixth MLS Cup title |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/la-galaxy-legend-landon-donovan-wins-mls-record-sixth-mls-cup-title |work=MLSsoccer.com |accessdate=November 6, 2022 |archive-date=November 7, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221107045429/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/la-galaxy-legend-landon-donovan-wins-mls-record-sixth-mls-cup-title |url-status=live }}</ref>

The highest recorded attendance for the MLS Cup was set in the [[MLS Cup 2018|2018 final]], with 73,019 spectators at [[Mercedes-Benz Stadium]] in [[Atlanta]], Georgia.<ref name="USA-ATL18">{{cite news |last=Reineking |first=Jim |date=December 8, 2018 |title=Atlanta United wins MLS Cup in just its second season |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/12/08/atlanta-united-wins-mls-cup-portland-timbers/2236263002/ |work=USA Today |access-date=December 8, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209062149/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/12/08/atlanta-united-wins-mls-cup-portland-timbers/2236263002/ |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> From 1996 to 2008, the English broadcast of the MLS Cup was carried in the United States on terrestrial network [[ESPN on ABC|ABC]]; it was moved to sister channel [[ESPN]] for the following seven editions.<ref name="AP-ABC2019">{{cite news |last=Reedy |first=Joe |date=August 28, 2019 |title=MLS Cup returning to ABC for first time since 2008 |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/tv/mls-cup-returning-to-abc-for-first-time-since-2008/2019/08/28/c128cafc-c9ad-11e9-9615-8f1a32962e04_story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830041704/https://www.washingtonpost.com/entertainment/tv/mls-cup-returning-to-abc-for-first-time-since-2008/2019/08/28/c128cafc-c9ad-11e9-9615-8f1a32962e04_story.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 30, 2019 |work=The Washington Post |agency=Associated Press |access-date=August 29, 2019}}</ref> From 2015 to 2022, ESPN and [[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox]] held rights to alternating editions of the cup;<ref>{{cite news |last=Tannenwald |first=Jonathan |date=May 11, 2014 |title=MLS, U.S. Soccer officially announce new TV deal with ESPN, Fox, Univision |url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/blogs/thegoalkeeper/Live-MLS-US-Soccer-officially-announce-new-TV-deal-with-ESPN-Fox-Univision.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=August 29, 2019 |archive-date=August 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830031827/https://www.inquirer.com/philly/blogs/thegoalkeeper/Live-MLS-US-Soccer-officially-announce-new-TV-deal-with-ESPN-Fox-Univision.html |url-status=live }}</ref> the 2019 cup, originally slated to be broadcast on ESPN, was moved to ABC.<ref name="AP-ABC2019"/> The Spanish language rights for the MLS Cup in the U.S. were awarded to [[Univision]] in 2007 and the match was aired on their various networks until 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stewart |first=Larry |date=February 7, 2007 |title=National TV to focus on Beckham and Galaxy |page=D3 |work=Los Angeles Times |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/113075970/national-tv-to-focus-on-beckham-and/ |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |accessdate=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114233157/https://www.newspapers.com/clip/113075970/national-tv-to-focus-on-beckham-and/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kennedy |first=Paul |date=December 10, 2013 |title=MLS Cup viewers on UniMas surpass those on ESPN |url=https://www.socceramerica.com/publications/article/55322/mls-cup-viewers-on-unimas-surpass-those-on-espn.html |work=[[Soccer America]] |url-access=limited |accessdate=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114233202/https://www.socceramerica.com/publications/article/55322/mls-cup-viewers-on-unimas-surpass-those-on-espn.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The U.S. linear television rights beginning in 2023 are held by Fox in English and [[Fox Deportes]] in Spanish; the MLS Cup final will air on those channels as well as [[Apple TV+]]'s [[MLS Season Pass]] streaming service worldwide.<ref>{{cite news |date=December 13, 2022 |title=MLS on linear TV: FOX Sports, TelevisaUnivision, TSN & RDS reach multi-year deals |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-on-linear-tv-fox-sports-televisaunivision-tsn-rds-reach-multi-year-deals |work=MLSsoccer.com |accessdate=December 13, 2022 |archive-date=December 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221213174846/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-on-linear-tv-fox-sports-televisaunivision-tsn-rds-reach-multi-year-deals |url-status=live }}</ref> In Canada, the MLS Cup has been broadcast in English by [[The Sports Network|TSN]] since 2011 and in French by [[TVA Sports]] since 2017.<ref>{{cite news |date=January 10, 2017 |title=Major League Soccer announces five-year deals with TSN, TVA Sports |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/soccer/major-league-soccer-announces-five-year-deals-with-tsn-tva-sports/article33564118/ |work=[[The Globe and Mail]] |agency=[[The Canadian Press]] |accessdate=November 14, 2022 |archive-date=November 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114234530/https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/soccer/major-league-soccer-announces-five-year-deals-with-tsn-tva-sports/article33564118/ |url-status=live }}</ref> The largest television audience for an MLS Cup broadcast was the [[MLS Cup 2016|2016 final]], which drew 3.5&nbsp;million viewers in the United States and Canada.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stejskal |first=Sam |date=December 13, 2016 |title=MLS Cup 2016 sets record for most-watched title game in league history |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-cup-2016-sets-record-most-watched-title-game-league-history |work=MLSsoccer.com |accessdate=November 8, 2022 |archive-date=November 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108155133/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/mls-cup-2016-sets-record-most-watched-title-game-league-history |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Inquirer-Ratings">{{cite news |last=Tannenwald |first=Jonathan |date=November 8, 2022 |title=Philadelphia helped MLS Cup draw its biggest U.S. TV audience in 25 years |url=https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/mls-cup-tv-ratings-philadelphia-los-angeles-20221108.html |work=The Philadelphia Inquirer |accessdate=November 8, 2022 |archive-date=November 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221108171226/https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/mls-cup-tv-ratings-philadelphia-los-angeles-20221108.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Results by team==
{{As of|2025}}, 33 teams have played in the league,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jenkins |first=Keith |date=February 27, 2025 |title=When did MLS teams begin playing? Key years to know |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/43937516/when-did-mls-teams-begin-playing-key-years-know |access-date=December 11, 2025 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> 21 of whom have appeared in an MLS Cup final, including 16 that have won a championship.<ref name="ESPN-List"/><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sigal |first=Jonathan |date=December 6, 2025 |title=CHAMPIONS! Inter Miami & Lionel Messi win MLS Cup over Vancouver Whitecaps |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/playoffs/2025/news/champions-inter-miami-lionel-messi-win-mls-cup-over-vancouver-whitecaps |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=MLS |language=en}}</ref> The [[LA Galaxy]] has appeared at and won the MLS Cup the most times, with six championships in ten appearances.<ref name="ESPN-List"/> The [[New England Revolution]] has appeared five times as a finalist, but has not won an MLS Cup.<ref name="ESPN-List"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Parker |first1=Graham |last2=Whittall |first2=Richard |date=December 8, 2014 |title=MLS Cup: how LA Galaxy crushed dreams of the Revolution |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2014/dec/08/mls-cup-how-la-galaxy-crushed-dreams-of-the-revolution |work=The Guardian |access-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625021639/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2014/dec/08/mls-cup-how-la-galaxy-crushed-dreams-of-the-revolution |archive-date=June 25, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The [[Chicago Fire FC|Chicago Fire]] won the MLS Cup in their inaugural season in [[1998 Major League Soccer season|1998]]; the only previous professional American soccer team to win a league championship in their inaugural season was the [[Philadelphia Atoms]] in the 1973 [[North American Soccer League (1968–1984)|NASL]] season.<ref name="USA-Numbers">{{cite news |last=Reineking |first=Jim |date=November 30, 2018 |title=2018 MLS Cup: Atlanta United vs. Portland Timbers by the numbers |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/11/30/mls-cup-2018-atlanta-united-vs-portland-timbers-story-lines/2159561002/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181209172345/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/11/30/mls-cup-2018-atlanta-united-vs-portland-timbers-story-lines/2159561002/ |archive-date=December 9, 2018 |access-date=December 10, 2018 |work=USA Today}}</ref>

==Stadiums==
[[File:LA Galaxy vs Houston Dynamo- Western Conference Finals panorama.jpg|thumb|right|The [[Dignity Health Sports Park]], home of the [[LA Galaxy]], has hosted seven editions of the MLS Cup|alt=A stadium with a soccer field surrounded by a full crowd. The field is lit with large floodlights above the stands.]]

From 1996 to 2011, the MLS Cup was hosted by a neutral site selected before the start of the season in a manner similar to the [[National Football League]]'s [[Super Bowl]] championship. Three teams advanced to the final after being named as hosts: [[D.C. United]] in 1997, the [[New England Revolution]] in 2002, and the [[LA Galaxy]] in 2011.<ref>{{cite news |last=McCarthy |first=Kyle |date=December 3, 2015 |title=MLS 101: Why is MLS Cup in Columbus? |url=https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/inside-mls/story/mls-cup-columbus-crew-sc-portland-timbers-hosting-rights-feature-120315 |work=[[Fox Sports (United States)|Fox Sports]] |access-date=February 11, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180212142203/https://www.foxsports.com/soccer/inside-mls/story/mls-cup-columbus-crew-sc-portland-timbers-hosting-rights-feature-120315 |archive-date=February 12, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Goff |first=Steven |date=March 8, 2012 |title=Major League Soccer 2012 preview |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/major-league-soccer-2012-preview/2012/03/08/gIQAXOIrzR_story.html |work=The Washington Post |access-date=December 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181210111000/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/major-league-soccer-2012-preview/2012/03/08/gIQAXOIrzR_story.html |archive-date=December 10, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Since the [[MLS Cup 2012|2012 edition]], the match has been hosted by the finalist with the highest regular season standing.<ref name="USA-2012"/> Several teams with smaller or inadequate stadiums have also considered using larger [[American football]] stadiums to host the MLS Cup, but all post-2012 editions have been played at regular MLS venues.<ref>{{cite news |last=Almond |first=Elliott |date=October 4, 2012 |title=San Jose Earthquakes mull stadium options for MLS Cup |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2012/10/04/san-jose-earthquakes-mull-stadium-options-for-mls-cup/ |work=[[The Mercury News]] |access-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624232806/https://www.mercurynews.com/2012/10/04/san-jose-earthquakes-mull-stadium-options-for-mls-cup/ |archive-date=June 24, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> The move towards a non-neutral venue was deemed a risk due to the cold November and December weather in some northern cities, as well as the lack of adequate stadiums for some teams.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goff |first=Steven |date=November 26, 2012 |title=MLS Cup at home comes with risk |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/soccer-insider/wp/2012/11/26/mls-cup-at-home-comes-with-risk/ |work=The Washington Post |access-date=June 24, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180725124317/https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/soccer-insider/wp/2012/11/26/mls-cup-at-home-comes-with-risk/ |archive-date=July 25, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref>

{{As of|2023}}, the MLS Cup has been hosted in 14 stadiums across 10 metropolitan areas in the United States and Canada.<ref name="Guide2023">{{cite web |date=December 2023 |title=2023 MLS Cup Game Guide |pages=8–9, 45–46 |url=https://mlssoccer.app.box.com/s/b50cp7q3nxhu5kaagear9ff8wopeuvue |publisher=Major League Soccer |accessdate=December 6, 2023 |archive-date=December 7, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231207180501/https://mlssoccer.app.box.com/s/b50cp7q3nxhu5kaagear9ff8wopeuvue |url-status=live }}</ref>{{Update inline|date=December 2025}} [[Dignity Health Sports Park]], previously named the Home Depot Center and StubHub Center, in [[Carson, California]], has hosted the MLS Cup the most times of any venue, with eight editions between 2003 and 2024. The [[Los Angeles metropolitan area]] has hosted the MLS Cup nine times at three venues: the [[Rose Bowl (stadium)|Rose Bowl]], Dignity Health Sports Park, and [[Banc of California Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Anderson |first=Jason |date=December 1, 2024 |title=MLS Cup 2024: LA Galaxy to face New York Red Bulls |url=https://prosoccerwire.usatoday.com/story/sports/mls/2024/12/01/mls-cup-2024-la-galaxy-new-york-red-bulls/76681759007/ |work=USA Today |department=Pro Soccer Wire |accessdate=December 7, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Lewis |first=Michael |date=October 31, 2022 |title=A Quick Look Ahead: To MLS Cup match-up between LAFC and Philadelphia |url=https://www.frontrowsoccer.com/2022/10/31/a-look-ahead-to-mls-match-up-between-lafc-and-philadelphia/ |work=Front Row Soccer |accessdate=December 7, 2024}}</ref> The largest attendance for an MLS Cup final was the [[MLS Cup 2018|2018 edition]] at [[Mercedes-Benz Stadium]] in [[Atlanta]], Georgia, with 73,019 spectators;<ref name="USA-ATL18"/> the smallest was in [[MLS Cup 2020|2020]] at [[Mapfre Stadium]] in [[Columbus, Ohio]], with only 1,500 spectators allowed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="NYT-2020">{{cite news |last=Das |first=Andrew |date=December 12, 2020 |title=Columbus Wins M.L.S. Cup, the Final Stop on a Journey to Stay Put |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/12/sports/soccer/columbus-crew-mls-cup.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=December 22, 2020 |archive-date=October 23, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211023141100/https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/12/sports/soccer/columbus-crew-mls-cup.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Butler |first=Dylan |date=November 2, 2019 |title=After CenturyLink Field sellout, a look at the top MLS Cup attendances |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/11/02/what-are-top-mls-cup-attendances |work=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=November 2, 2019 |archive-date=November 3, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191103044549/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2019/11/02/what-are-top-mls-cup-attendances |url-status=live }}</ref> Three editions have been hosted outside the United States, all at [[BMO Field]] in [[Toronto]], Canada.<ref name="2017Guide"/> {{As of|2024}}, 11&nbsp;of the 14 editions under the non-neutral venue format have been won by the host team.<ref>{{cite news |last=Stone |first=Simon |date=December 6, 2025 |title=MLS Cup final: Thomas Muller out to spoil Inter Miami's title quest |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c04vdgdg2e3o |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |accessdate=December 7, 2025}}</ref>{{Update inline|date=December 2025}}
